chunks: Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Talhah ibn Zayd from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he did not validate the letter of a judge to another judge regarding a fixed punishment or anything else, until the Banu Umayyah took power, so they validated it with evidences.
ai.seo_question: How did the validation of judges' letters change from the time of Imam Ali to the Umayyad era?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) maintained a strict standard of judicial independence by refusing to accept the official letter (kitab) of one judge as conclusive evidence for another, thereby preventing administrative convenience from overriding rigorous proof. This practice shifted during the Umayyad era, where such letters were validated based on evidences (bayyinat), reflecting a broader transition in Islamic jurisprudence towards accepting written administrative records as binding proof in courts.
